rule:
(one cause per error; an error is a (file, document, kind) of lint/analyse.py's part (d) scoring):

1. Routing. The run was handed over unrouted (deferred) or routed to another type: every error of the file is a routing
   error, split by whether the file's defining event is stated false (denied-event file).
2-4. The file was routed to its type. Three replays through the product's evaluator (workflows.evaluate with checked=True,
   the inputs built as the product builds them: accepted established facts plus applicable presumptions; findings =
   documents present or unusable with an accepted verdict):
   D  = designed fact states + designed attachment states (exactly as generator/reference.py builds the reference);
   PD = the product's fact states + designed attachment states;
   DP = designed fact states + the product's document findings;
   PP = the product's facts and findings (must reproduce the stored plan; checked).
   If D already differs from reference.json for the document: cause 4 (workflow differs from reference).
   Else if PD shows the error and DP does not: cause 2 (fact reading). Else if DP shows the error and PD does not:
   cause 3 (document judgment). If both show it: each alone suffices; counted under cause 2 and flagged "also document".
   If neither shows it but PP does: the two together; counted under cause 2 and flagged "joint".
   The fact named for cause 2 is the fact whose correction alone (product state replaced by the designed state, all other
   product states kept, designed attachments) removes the error; where several do, the first in workflow order is named
   and the others listed; where none alone does, "several facts jointly".
   What the product did with the fact, from its recorded state and the three stored reading responses:
   - admitted the wrong value: established (all readings agreed, quotations located) a value other than the designed one;
   - readings disagreed and it held although the file states the fact: designed stated, product unresolved, and at least
     one reading gave the designed value or answered open (sub-pattern: the three verdicts);
   - read a stated fact as not stated: designed stated, and no reading gave a value or answered open (a presumption,
     where the fact has one, then filled the other value);
   - read an open fact as settled: designed open, product established a value or a presumption filled it;
   - read an unmentioned fact as open: designed not mentioned, product unresolved (a reading gave a value or answered
     open, so no presumption filled it).
5. Scoring convention: a need outside the type's catalogue (a process-builder addition) or an optional document. (On
   these runs the process builder added nothing and no optional document produced an error; the class is kept for the
   rule's completeness and for the revised re-run.)
6. Text and recorded state plausibly disagree: a cause-2 error is moved here when (a) the file was kept as read and the
   blind check changed this fact's state (design.json facts_designed) and the product's reading matches the original
   design, or (b) diagnosis_review.json records, after reading the file text, that the passage the readings quoted
   plausibly states what the product read (the judgment and its reason are listed).

routing.error: schema_mismatch: The model answer did not match its schema: $.facts: array length outside bounds (2 items; allowed 0 to 1)

review_notes: Owner classes used for the planner's question: 'rule wording' = a question, not_this or routing wording of ours that this revision may change; 'must_show wording' = a must_show item of ours that this revision may not change; 'product' = the product's reading, quotation, combination or document judgment; 'benchmark design' = the file design or the reference, not the product and not a changeable wording; 'text vs recorded state' = the file text plausibly supports what the product read (cause 6).

Routing: for a non-denied file the judgment names why the routing reading answered as it did; for a denied-event file it says what the product did and whether an empty plan is what the rule text gives.
level0_text: Why dismissal is worst at share level 0 (no designed open fact): 24 errors in 15 files, 18 of them holds where the file settles the fact, and 16 of the 24 sit in four files. 11 holds come from three files in which every reading gave the designed value but one or more quotations were not found word for word in the uploaded text, so the product left the fact unresolved: dis_32d79153a27f (the defining event employer_gave_notice; one reading began its quotation with a capital 'We are terminating' where the letter has 'we are terminating'), dis_b7f5c9e07c99 (the defining event dismissed_immediately; one reading quoted 'mmediate' for the scan-noised 'irnmediate') and dis_408b774aa7db (notice_period_ended; two readings corrected the scan noise in 'läuft noc'). A held defining event holds every document of the type, which is why two files give 8 holds. 3 holds are the routing of dis_c50430dbdfa1 (rule wording), 3 holds and 2 requests are the denied-event file dis_ff1e9056d2c3 routed to wrongful_termination (benchmark design: its denial is an ordinary notice, the defining event of types 1 and 2), and 1 hold is a misreading (dis_fcbd44dfcef3, one reading of three took 'Ich war schon krank, als die Kündigung kam' as notice before the protected period). Level 0 is not harder by design; the excess is the concentration of these four files (with 15 files in the level, each error adds 0.07 errors per file).
measures_text: measures_pending causes none of the 67 theft errors: no document hangs on the instruction step (h_instruction / a_instruction), and the product defers only on facts that change a document, so an unresolved measures_pending holds nothing. Its low admission where stated true (3 of 9 files the runs read: 2 of 5 simple_theft_away, 1 of 4 theft_at_home) comes from what the pending measures are. Admitted: blocking a phone by its IMEI, blocking a credit card, marking a laptop as stolen and locking it through its user account (all three stop the thief using the item). Not admitted: registering a bicycle's frame number on stolen-bike lists 'in case it turns up' (3 files: not stated or false, presumed false), reporting a camera's or laptop's serial number to the maker so that it is noticed at a repair (2 files: one reading of three not stated, held), going with the police to secure a bicycle found for sale (1 file: held). The question's not_this excludes 'steps to find the thief or recover the items', and the theft workflows append the not_this to the question the product reads; the writer and the blind check saw the question only (writer bundles and blind-check inputs carry no not_this), so the designs count recovery steps as measures to reduce the loss and the product, following our not_this, does not. The exclusion of steps to recover the items has no passage: VVG Art. 38a Abs. 1 asks the claimant to reduce the loss ('für Minderung des Schadens zu sorgen'), which getting stolen items back does. That is a defect of our wording (narrower than the passage), fixed in Part B; it changes no document and no reference.
frontier_text: Frontier partial run (gpt-6.1-terra, clean, tenancy, the first 39 files in manifest order): 5 routing failures, all unrouted. Four are denied-event files (ten_429b182434cf, ten_776e0e61986b, ten_8572ddc89110, ten_8c54d4a61b0a): no type's defining event holds and the empty plan is what the rule text gives (0 errors each). One is ten_580485dac025, whose defining event increase_applied is designed open (the file leaves open whether a higher rent was announced or demanded), so the routing question has no answer in the text (benchmark design; the cost-efficient model routed it). The failed run, ten_5aecbb73131b, is a product failure: the routing answer gave two facts where its schema allows one, and the run stopped. The three tenancy files that the cost-efficient model routed wrongly for wording reasons (ten_c2a72cbf1698, ten_b4d4cb05336f, ten_e4858b3af131) are outside the 39 files run.
limits: DEVELOPMENT, post hoc, not a result. One run per file on the cost-efficient model; 176 files (59 tenancy, 59 theft, 58 dismissal); small counts per cause.

The cause attribution is mechanical (replays through the product's evaluator); the owner classification is partly a reading of the files by the same session that proposes the wording fixes (diagnosis_review.json). A second reader should check both.
A hold or request can have two sufficient causes; such errors are counted once under fact reading and flagged ('also document', 'joint').
The routing reading's own reasoning is not stored; for 'other' and null answers the cause is inferred from the question wording and the quotation the router gave.
Reading verdicts come from the cached responses as lint/analyse.py parses them (a requote retry replaces the first answer).
